monthly_review.summary: You've significantly increased training intensity this month while maintaining volume consistency, evidenced by faster pace, higher HR, elevated aerobic TE, and a marked shift toward higher HR zones — especially Zones 3–4.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 3–4 HR time increased from 48% last month to 50% this month, while Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 30% — indicating a clear strategic shift toward threshold and moderate-intensity work, likely driving the pace and TE improvements.

goal_tracker.message: You need 12.6 more km across 3 additional sessions in the remaining 17 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~4.2 km per session.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.28 to 13.62 km/hr per bpm even as average HR rose +7 bpm and pace quickened — suggesting better cardiovascular economy at higher workloads, supported by stable cadence and improved stride length on your fastest run (90.77 cm at 7:25/km on 2026-04-12).

insights.title: Zone 2 underutilized; risk of aerobic base erosion
insights.body: Zone 2 time dropped sharply from 47% (last month) to 30% (this month), while Zone 3–4 rose to 50% — meaning only 11% of this month’s time was spent in true recovery/easy aerobic zone (Z1+Z2), below the ideal 70–80% for sustainable endurance development in recreational runners.

insights.title: Cadence stability masks stride variability
insights.body: Avg cadence held steady at 150 spm, but stride length varied widely — from 70.96 cm (slowest run, 9:00/km) to 90.77 cm (fastest run, 7:25/km) — indicating appropriate neuromuscular adaptation to pace, though ground contact time remained stable (~307 ms), suggesting no fatigue-induced form breakdown.

insights.title: High-intensity density without volume buffer
insights.body: You achieved a 4.6 Aerobic TE (near-maximal for your profile) on 2026-04-12 — your highest single-run TE — yet followed it with only one 4.0 km run at low HR (141 bpm) before today; no dedicated recovery or Z1 session occurred in the past 5 runs, increasing cumulative strain risk.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-minute Zone 1–2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) within next 48 hours, aiming for avg HR 132 bpm and pace ~9:30–10:00/km.
recommendations.reason: To restore Z1+Z2 time to ≥40% of monthly volume and offset the current 11% — critical for autonomic recovery and aerobic base resilience, especially after a 4.6 TE session.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 × 8-minute Zone 3 tempo at 152–158 bpm (avg pace ~7:50–8:10/km) with 90 sec walk/jog recovery, keeping cadence ≥152 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 3 % rose to 26% and recent runs show strong efficiency at sub-threshold paces (e.g., 8:07/km @ 149 bpm on 2026-04-03); this session targets lactate clearance without overreaching.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-sec strides off a 5km easy run (HR <130 bpm), focusing on lifting knees and landing midfoot — monitor vertical oscillation target ≤7.5 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your vertical oscillation averaged 8.2 cm across recent runs, and lowest value was 7.8 cm (on two slower runs); reducing it further improves efficiency — strides are low-risk neuromuscular primers.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild Z1/Z2 volume to support high-intensity gains, while refining form economy through targeted drills and controlled tempos.
